title: GRADIENT ASCENT

intro.headline: Climb to the highest reward
intro.body: Same engine, flipped sign. The curve is now a reward landscape and the update climbs instead of descends. This is what policy-gradient methods do: nudge the parameter in whichever direction increases expected reward.

messages.converged: Converged — the gradient is ~0. The policy has stopped improving; it sits on a local reward peak.
messages.diverged: Diverged — the step size is too large, the policy blew past the edge of the landscape.
messages.tooSlow: Barely moving — reward is climbing steeply but each update is tiny. Training would take forever.

insight: Peaked at θ = {x} with reward {value} after {steps} steps at step size {rate}. Ascent and descent are the same algorithm with one sign flipped — the engine drawing this landscape is byte-identical to the gradient-descent game. Starting somewhere else lands you on a different peak, which is exactly why RL runs are seed-sensitive.
